title: Coherent monoidal descent of an exact adjoint equivalence
statement: Let $A,B$ be braided monoidal closed Grothendieck abelian categories with additive tensor and functorial flat resolutions, and use their ordinary K-flat unbounded derived tensor products [def-kun-derived-tensor]. Let $F:A\to B$ and $G:B\to A$ be additive strong monoidal equivalences and $F\dashv G$ an adjunction with invertible unit and counit and monoidal counit. Then the exact induced functors $D(F),D(G)$ admit strong monoidal structures such that the canonical localization comparisons $Q_A D(F)\cong F_{\mathrm{Ch}}Q_B$ and $Q_B D(G)\cong G_{\mathrm{Ch}}Q_A$ are monoidal natural isomorphisms, and the unit and counit of the termwise descended adjunction $D(F)\dashv D(G)$ are monoidal.

source.place: Tag 06YS, lemma-K-flat-resolution, with the normalized derived comparison argument of etale-cohomology.tex, Tag 0F0F, lemma-projection-formula-proper, expressed for abstract exact monoidal equivalences.

proof.text: A strong monoidal equivalence preserves flat objects, colimits and acyclic complexes. Apply the existing functorial flat resolution in both categories to find K-flat representatives whose images are K-flat. The left-derived tensor comparison is invertible on these representatives. Its associativity and unit equations descend by the universal property of localization. In Lean this is leftDerivedTensorComparison and OplaxMonoidal.ofLaxSquare; transport along leftDerivedFunctorIsoMapDerivedCategory. The defining square proves that the canonical homotopy-to-derived factor is monoidal.

Give the induced right functors on homotopy and derived categories their right-adjoint lax structures. The unit and counit are invertible, so those structures are strong and the adjunctions are monoidal. The counit on complexes is monoidal: its unit equation is the original unit equation in degree zero; its tensor equation follows on each direct-sum summand from tensor naturality and the original counit tensor equation.

Write the right mate of the left localization square as the composite of the upper unit, the left comparison, and the lower counit. It is monoidal. The compatibility formula for the termwise descended adjunction identifies it with the inverse of the specified right comparison, by naturality and the right triangle identity. Thus the right comparison is monoidal. Compose each quotient and localization square to obtain the canonical comparisons from complexes; their component formulas agree with mapDerivedCategoryFactors.
